description: Compute the Even-winning region of a bounded finite parity game using Zielonka's recursive attractor algorithm.

source.title: Parity Games
source.algorithm_reference_title: Infinite Games Played on Finite Graphs
source.license: Copyright remains with the cited publishers; clean-room algorithm description only.

contract.operation: Return the complete Even-winning vertex region for a finite total directed parity game.
contract.player_encoding: Owner 0 is Even and owner 1 is Odd.
contract.parity_convention: The minimum priority occurring infinitely often determines the winner; Even wins an even minimum and Odd wins an odd minimum, following Chapter 591.
contract.algorithm: Choose the minimum active priority, attract its parity-matching player to all vertices of that priority, recurse outside the attractor, and either return that region or compute the opponent attractor and recurse again.
contract.tie_rule: Every vertex with the minimum active priority enters the target set together. Attractor growth scans ascending vertex IDs and repeats to a fixed point; the returned partition is independent of this scan order.
contract.output_encoding: One signed 64-bit integer with bit v set exactly when vertex v belongs to Even's winning region; the Odd region is the complement among vertices 0..N-1.
contract.strategy_output: Winning strategies are excluded; the benchmark target is Algorithm 1's winning partition.

input.edges: Directed simple arcs; duplicate arcs are rejected, and every vertex has at least one outgoing arc.

workspace.meaning: Fixed adjacency bitmasks and recursion state for at most eight vertices and twenty arcs.
